– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test involves extensive checks of type assignability between various generic list types with different parameterizations, including wildcards, bounds, and arrays of generics. The relevant method under test is TypeUtils.isAssignable(Type, Type) which delegates to an overloaded method with an additional Map parameter (typeVarAssigns) for tracking type variable assignments.

Inspection of the isAssignable(Type, Type, Map) method shows that it dispatches the type check based on the runtime type of the "toType" argument, calling helper methods depending on whether "toType" is a Class, ParameterizedType, GenericArrayType, WildcardType, or TypeVariable.

For ParameterizedType handling, TypeUtils.isAssignable(Type, ParameterizedType, Map) uses TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class, Map) to determine the type argument mappings of the "type" relative to the raw class of the "toParameterizedType". Similarly, it obtains the type argument mappings from the target ParameterizedType and compares each corresponding type argument for assignability.

The crucial helper method TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class, Map) recursively extracts the mapping of formal type variables to actual type arguments for the input "type" when seen as an instance of "toClass" or a subtype thereof. This method delegates to an overloaded helper for ParameterizedType, Class, GenericArrayType, WildcardType, or TypeVariable types. The retrieved Map encodes which actual types correspond to which formal type variables in the class or interface inheritance hierarchy.

Relevant to the current bug report and failing test is the observation that getTypeArguments() has known bugs with partially-assigned classes. Specifically, for classes where only some type parameters are assigned (e.g., a generic supertype is partially specified), getTypeArguments() may skip or fail to properly record the type argument mappings. This would cause isAssignable() to incorrectly determine assignability involving such partially-parameterized types.

The test exercises cases with partially-assigned generic types, including wildcards with bounds, and arrays of parameterized types, which likely trigger the missing mappings problem. The recent bug report summary and code confirm this: "TypeUtils.getTypeArguments() misses type arguments for partially-assigned classes".

The method getTypeArguments(ParameterizedType, Class, Map) constructs the type variable assignment map by recursively traversing owner types and the inheritance chain, but in its loop mapping type args to parameters, it conditionally replaces entries only if the RHS type argument is itself already mapped in the map. This logic, shown here:

    typeVarAssigns.put(typeParams[i], typeVarAssigns.containsKey(typeArg) ? typeVarAssigns.get(typeArg) : typeArg);

may fail to propagate some type variable assignments correctly for partial assignments, leading to incomplete maps. Consequently, isAssignable underestimates type assignability in these cases.

This explains why the failing test highlighted mismatches (false negatives) for assignability between parameterized generic types with partially bound parameters. The core issue lies in getTypeArguments() returning incomplete type argument maps due to neglecting some partially assigned type variables during map construction. This defeats accurate assignment checks in isAssignable().

The recent bug report illustrates this exact scenario and confirms the diagnosis.

Summary:
- isAssignable delegates to getTypeArguments to resolve type variable assignments.
- getTypeArguments misses some partial type argument mappings for partially assigned classes.
- This causes isAssignable to return false negatives in assignability tests with parameterized generic types.
- The test reflects this with multiple failed isAssignable assertions.
- The bug lies in getTypeArguments focusing only on fully resolved type arguments but missing to propagate partial assignments properly when building the mapping.
- This leads to incomplete type variable assignments maps, causing isAssignable to fail on some generic type assignability checks.

This diagnosis matches both the observed test failure behavior and the recent report context.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
